After the conclusion of the "Imperial Durbar" in Delhi, a royal proclamation was read at the foot of the memorial column in Trafalgar Square, announcing that Queen Victoria was granted the title "Empress of India." No ruler in India had received the imperial crown since the Mughal Emperor was deposed by the British East India Company. After the company's power was dissolved, a view spread widely that the Queen's superiority over the Indian princes should be confirmed in the form of an imperial title. Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli is believed to be the architect of this idea.
